Q: How can I make links with generic names like "Overview" in navigation structures most accessible? A:

For page names like "Overview" that are repeated multiple times in multiple sections, adding additional disambiguating text is helpful.

The first rule of ARIA is to not rely on ARIA if there's a native way to achieve the same result. The aria-label attributes in this case are acceptable, but a better ARIA-less way to achieve the same things is with an sr-only (screen reader only) class like this:

<li><a href=""><span class="sr-only">Control System </span>Overview</a></li>

Adding disambiguation text for links that aren't repeated multiple times (like "API") could be annoyingly verbose. My advice would be: Consider if renaming "API" to "Unattended Operation API" would be helpful for all users (even those not relying on assistive tech), and then do (or don't do) that for all users.

Q: How to reset or change the passphrase for a GitHub SSH key? A:
  1. Log in to your github account.
  2. Go to the "Settings" page (the "wrench and screwdriver" icon in the top right corner of the page).
  3. Go to "SSH keys" page.
  4. Generate a new SSH key (probably studying the links provided by github on that page).
  5. Add your new key using the "Add SSH key" link.
  6. Verify your new key works.
  7. Make gitub forget your old key by using the "Delete" link next to it in the list of known keys.

Q: How can I place axis labels closer to a PolarAxis in Makie and remove the unused surrounding regions? A:

The blank white surrounding area appears to occur because f has size (500, 300) while pax has size (220,180). If they are the same the white area disappears.

In lieu of automatically positioned labels, one possible workaround is to use manually positioned labels. The labels default to the center, so adding a padding tuple (left, right, bottom, top) to the label can be used to adjust the position of the text. For example, adding padding on the right will move the text to the left.

Limitations:

  • In this example, PolarAxis clip=false is used to make the labels visible outside the pie wedge.
  • If the labels with padding are too big the polar axis will become distorted.
using CairoMakie

let

    f = Figure(size = (200, 180))
    gl = f[1, 1] = GridLayout()

    rmax = 2.0
    θmin, θmax = -π/5, π/5

    pax = PolarAxis(
        gl[1, 1];
        width = 200, height = 180,
        thetalimits = (θmin, θmax),
        theta_0 = π/2,
        thetaticklabelsize = 12,
        rticklabelsize = 12,
        backgroundcolor = :pink,
        clip=false,
    )

    rlims!(pax, 0, rmax)

    label_SE = Label(f[1, 1], "SE", padding=(0, 135, 140, 0))
    label_voltage = Label(f[1,1], "Voltage [μV]", rotation=π/2+θmin, padding=(120,0,0,60))

    f
end

Julia v1.12.5, CairoMakie 0.15.9

Q: How can I get the Claude Code extension in Cursor IDE on Windows to use my Conda Python interpreter specified in AGENTS.md? A:

From the official Claude documentation:

  1. Document requirements: Clearly specify dependencies and commands in your CLAUDE.md file. If you have an AGENTS.md file, you can source it in your CLAUDE.md using @AGENTS.md to maintain a single source of truth.

I created a CLAUDE.md file that only contains @AGENTS.md and it works fine.

Q: Linux stop a command while its loading in PUTTY/SSH A:

use nohup. example:

nohup ./foobar.sh & < /dev/null > ./log 2>&1 
exit

In foobar.sh you can have the following content

command you wish to execute

sleep <no of seconds>

or you can use "screen", you need to install "screen" in you host, then

> screen {your-cmd}

and press ctrl+A followed ctrl+D detach current (but your cmd still running) session .

Q: how to do the dssc diff between versions with latest and latest-1 version A:

so far the diff can be done via simpler coding:

dssc diff file_name -ver last_but_one

i.e. the specified version versus the latest one.

Q: Does Android 4.2.2 support usb bluetooth dongle? A:

CyanogenMod and Android-X86 contain patches to support USB HCI like this: http://review.cyanogenmod.org/#/c/45537/

http://review.cyanogenmod.org/#/c/45538/

http://git.android-x86.org/?p=platform/external/bluetooth/bluedroid.git;a=commit;h=471bdeac2ffe054221b3eab72e3b87523c0aa97c

To enable this support in board look at android-x86 example, for BoardConfig

# Some framework code requires this to enable BT
BOARD_HAVE_BLUETOOTH := true
BLUETOOTH_HCI_USE_USB := true
BOARD_HAVE_BLUETOOTH_BCM := true
BOARD_BLUETOOTH_BDROID_BUILDCFG_INCLUDE_DIR := device/generic/x86/bluetooth

and for buildcfg 

#ifndef _BDROID_BUILDCFG_H
#define _BDROID_BUILDCFG_H 
#define BTM_DEF_LOCAL_NAME "Android-x86"
// At present either USB or UART is supported
#define BLUETOOTH_HCI_USE_USB          TRUE
// Bluetooth Low Power Mode is supported on BT4.0
#define HCILP_INCLUDED                 FALSE
#endif

Also your kernel need UHID support.
